v1.feedback: The Oldenburg soft-sculpture concept maps well onto L-system tips, and the stochastic branching gives real structural variety — but the marshmallow blob radius (0.55–0.9 units) is likely too small relative to the tree's ~14-unit height to read as a deliberate 'puff' rather than fuzzy tip noise; double the cluster sphere radius and add a distinct warm hue shift (cream/pink) in the fragment shader so the marshmallow volumes pop against the woody trunk palette. The tipness smoothstep gate (2.0–4.5) should be validated against actual max gen from the expansion depth — if depth is only 4, most particles barely enter the morph range, making the swerve invisible at default camera. Consider scaling point size up for marshmallow particles so they coalesce into readable soft masses rather than dispersed additive glow.

v2.feedback: The marshmallow-puff cycle on L-system tips is a genuine swerve — readable, playful, and structurally tied to the branching grammar rather than sprinkled on as post-process noise. The 10-second inflate/hold/deflate timing is well-paced but the puff radius (1.6) makes the clusters read as generic spherical blobs; shaping them as slightly squashed oblates or toasting the top hemisphere darker would sell 'marshmallow' more convincingly. The bark-to-cream palette transition during puff is tasteful, though the additive blending washes out the cream into near-white at density peaks — try a softer blend mode or clamp the alpha so the pastel tint survives. Camera framing and tree scale are solid, filling the frame well with clear silhouette.
